# DelphiR

DelphiR is an R package for the statistical analysis of Delphi studies.
It imports and validates the expert ratings, computes descriptive
statistics by item, round and indicator, assesses consensus and
stability, identifies the items to be submitted to a further round,
draws publication-quality figures and generates a complete round report
in HTML or Word format.

## Installation

The development version can be installed from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("yuricalleo/DelphiR")
```

## Data format

Ratings are arranged with one row per expert, one column per item and
one numeric rating in each cell:

| expert | round | indicator | E1  | E2  | E3  |
|--------|-------|-----------|-----|-----|-----|
| EXP01  | 1     | impact    | 9   | 7   | 5   |
| EXP02  | 1     | impact    | 6   | 5   | 7   |
| EXP03  | 1     | impact    | 8   |     | 6   |

- Empty cells denote missing ratings.
- The expert identifier is required to follow the same expert across
  rounds.
- The round and indicator columns are optional. Without them, each table
  is treated as a single round and a single indicator, and tables can be
  combined with
  [`delphi_bind()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_bind.md).
- Each indicator has its own rating scale, for example from 1 to 10 or
  from 1 to 100.

[`delphi_template()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_template.md)
creates an empty Excel or CSV file in this format, with instructions and
the code needed to import it. Ratings in long format, with one row per
rating, are imported with
[`delphi_data_long()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_data_long.md)
or `read_delphi(layout = "long")`, and survey exports with two header
rows (indicators in the first row, item statements in the second) with
`read_delphi(header_rows = 2)`. When identifiers do not denote the same
expert in every round, as with response numbers of separate
questionnaires, the data should be declared with `linked = FALSE`, so
that rounds are compared as independent samples.

## Example

``` r

library(DelphiR)

# Empty template to be filled in
delphi_template("my_delphi.xlsx", items = 12)

# Example data: two rounds, two indicators
x <- delphi_data(
  delphi_example,
  expert_col = "expert", round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
  scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100))
)

x                    # overview
summary(x)           # panel and median [IQR] by item and round
delphi_describe(x)   # descriptive statistics
delphi_consensus(x)  # consensus: IQR at most 20% of the rating scale
delphi_stability(x)  # stability between consecutive rounds
delphi_status(x)     # item status and items for the next round

# Figures, returned as ggplot objects
plot(x, type = "distribution", indicator = "impact")
plot(x, type = "trend", indicator = "impact")
plot(x, type = "consensus")
plot(x, type = "map")

# Round report in Word or HTML format
delphi_report(x, "round2_report.docx")
```

See
[`vignette("DelphiR")`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/articles/DelphiR.md)
for an introduction to the complete workflow.

## Consensus and stability

By default, an item reaches consensus when its interquartile range (IQR)
does not exceed 20% of the rating scale (von der Gracht, 2012). The
scale is measured by its number of points, so that the threshold
corresponds to an IQR of at most 1 on a five-point scale and at most 2
on a ten-point scale.

Stability between consecutive rounds is assessed with the Wilcoxon test
(signed-rank for linked experts, rank-sum otherwise), with the 15%
change criterion of Scheibe, Skutsch and Schofer (1975), or with both.
Consensus and stability are then combined into four categories:

| Status             | Consensus | Stable | Further round |
|--------------------|-----------|--------|---------------|
| Consensus          | yes       | yes    | no            |
| Unstable consensus | yes       | no     | yes           |
| Stable dissent     | no        | yes    | no            |
| Open               | no        | no     | yes           |

## Citation

To cite DelphiR in publications, use `citation("DelphiR")`.

## References

Scheibe, M., Skutsch, M. and Schofer, J. (1975). Experiments in Delphi
methodology. In H. A. Linstone and M. Turoff (Eds.), *The Delphi Method:
Techniques and Applications* (pp. 262-287). Reading, MA: Addison-Wesley.

von der Gracht, H. A. (2012). Consensus measurement in Delphi studies:
Review and implications for future quality assurance. *Technological
Forecasting and Social Change*, 79(8), 1525-1536.
<https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techfore.2012.04.013>

# Package index

## Data import

- [`delphi_template()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_template.md)
  : Create a data-entry template
- [`read_delphi()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/read_delphi.md)
  : Read Delphi ratings from a file
- [`delphi_data()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_data.md)
  : Create a Delphi data object
- [`delphi_data_long()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_data_long.md)
  : Create a Delphi data object from a long table
- [`delphi_bind()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_bind.md)
  : Combine Delphi data objects
- [`is_delphi_data()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/is_delphi_data.md)
  : Check whether an object is a Delphi data object

## Description

- [`delphi_describe()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_describe.md)
  : Descriptive statistics of a Delphi study
- [`delphi_panel()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_panel.md)
  : Panel participation across rounds
- [`summary(`*`<delphi_data>`*`)`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/summary.delphi_data.md)
  : Summarise a Delphi data object
- [`print(`*`<delphi_data>`*`)`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/print.delphi_data.md)
  : Print a Delphi data object
- [`delphi_wide()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_wide.md)
  : Ratings in wide format
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<delphi_data>`*`)`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/as.data.frame.delphi_data.md)
  : Convert a Delphi data object to a data frame

## Consensus and stability

- [`delphi_consensus()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_consensus.md)
  : Consensus by item, round and indicator
- [`delphi_stability()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_stability.md)
  : Stability of ratings between rounds
- [`delphi_status()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_status.md)
  : Item status from consensus and stability

## Figures

- [`plot(`*`<delphi_data>`*`)`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/plot.delphi_data.md)
  : Plot a Delphi data object
- [`delphi_plot_distribution()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_plot_distribution.md)
  : Distribution of the ratings by round
- [`delphi_plot_trend()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_plot_trend.md)
  : Median and interquartile range across rounds
- [`delphi_plot_consensus()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_plot_consensus.md)
  : Consensus heat map
- [`delphi_plot_map()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_plot_map.md)
  : Two-indicator map of the items
- [`theme_delphi()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/theme_delphi.md)
  : ggplot2 theme for DelphiR figures

## Reports

- [`delphi_report()`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_report.md)
  : Generate a round report

## Data

- [`delphi_example`](https://yuricalleo.github.io/DelphiR/reference/delphi_example.md)
  : Example Delphi study
